title: Network geometry shapes the transformation of task representations across the human cortex
title_zh: 网络几何塑造人类皮层任务表征的转变
abstract: Flexible cognition requires the brain to generalize across tasks while preserving task-specific information. Previous work showed that task representations are compressed in the association cortex and expanded in sensory and motor systems, but the mechanisms underlying these transformations are unclear. Here we test whether the geometry of intrinsic brain connectivity constrains how representations change between cortical regions. We analyzed functional MRI acquired during 16 diverse cognitive tasks together with activity flow modeling, finding that connectivity dimensionality predicts representational changes across the cortex. Low-dimensional connectivity compressed task representations and increased similarities across tasks, whereas high-dimensional connectivity expanded representations and supported conjunctive coding of task features. Activity flow modeling reproduced the observed compression-to-expansion pattern along the sensory-association-motor hierarchy and generated representational geometries that more closely matched targets than sources, consistent with transformation rather than transfer of information. These findings identify network geometry as a systems-level principle that shapes cortical representations and supports flexible cognition.
abstract_zh: 灵活的认知需要大脑在概括跨任务的同时保留任务特异性信息。以往研究表明，任务表征在联合皮层被压缩，在感觉和运动系统中被扩展，但这些转变的机制尚不清楚。在此，我们测试内在脑连接几何是否约束了表征在皮层区域间的变化。我们在16种不同认知任务的功能磁共振成像数据基础上，结合活动流建模，发现连接维度预测了皮层中表征的变化。低维连接压缩任务表征并增加了跨任务相似性，而高维连接扩展表征并支持任务特征的联合编码。活动流建模重现了沿感觉-联合-运动层级观察到的压缩到扩展的模式，并生成的表征几何比源更接近目标，这与信息的转变而非转移一致。这些发现确定了网络几何作为塑造皮层表征并支持灵活认知的系统级原理。
